src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py:67-68 - line 67 says multi-row or 1-row-with->4-cols results are shown as a table outside the response and instructs NOT to repeat the table; line 68 says a 1-row result with <=4 columns is shown as short text and instructs to state the answer in a plain sentence. grep for 'DO NOT need'/'do not need to include'/'raw result' across the whole file returns no matches, confirming the old sentence is fully removed. src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py:68 tells the model, unconditionally of emit_text presence, to 'state the answer in a plain sentence in your response' for a qualifying one-row result. When emit_text is in the tool set, lines 113-135 add the ANSWER COMPOSITION block, whose line 123 states non-emit_text assistant text is hidden. This looks like it could conflict with line 68's instruction to 'state ... in your response' outside an emit_text call. However line 125 explicitly reconciles the two: 'For a one-row result shown as short text, DO use emit_text to state the answer in a plain sentence.' This line directly redirects the plain-sentence instruction into an emit_text call, so the composed prompt (both sections concatenated when has_emit_text is true) does not leave the model with conflicting instructions — the emit_text section supersedes/clarifies where the plain sentence must go.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1200-1216 (_small_result_to_markdown) returns None — i.e. falls back to the table block — whenever payload.get('truncated', 0) != 0, in addition to the row/column-count checks. So a 1-row, <=4-column result whose row was dropped by the per-block size budget (truncated==1) is rendered as a table, not short text. The system prompt line at src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py:68 ('When a query returns a single row with four or fewer columns, it is shown as short text rather than a table...') is unconditional and carries no qualification for this truncated case anywhere else in the file (checked lines 60-130, including the emit_text guidance at line 125). src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1200-1223 defines _small_result_to_markdown: it returns None unless len(rows)==1, payload['truncated']==0, and 1<=len(columns)<=_SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS. This matches AC1 exactly: 1 row, 1 column, truncated==0 -> one text block '**<column>:** <value>', no table block.

_small_result_to_markdown (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1200-1219) only ever receives payloads produced by _compute_table_payload (via _build_table_payload). In _compute_table_payload, coerced_rows is built as `[[_coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) for c in columns] for row in rows]` (line 908), i.e. each row list is constructed by iterating the `columns` list itself, using `.get(c, "")` as a safe default for any missing key. This guarantees every row in payload['rows'] has exactly len(columns) elements regardless of what keys the source row dict (e.g. from a DataFrameComponent with explicit columns differing from row dict keys) actually contains. Therefore zip(columns, rows[0], strict=True) at line 1219 can never encounter a length mismatch and never raises.

components_to_blocks builds candidates with a private '_is_answer' tag only for ctype==TEXT (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:320-329); DATAFRAME payloads that qualify as one-row/narrow become {'type':'result_text', 'text':small} candidates (lines 330-335) with no '_is_answer' key. After the loop, blocks pass through _trim_blocks_to_budget (line 478, defined at 1070-1116) which operates generically on the blocks list (byte-budget prefix trimming + truncation notice) with no special-casing by original candidate type, so the now-generic text blocks are trimmed the same as any other block, no different from a table/chart block. No code path drops or mistreats result_text/one-row text blocks as answer prose.

For DATAFRAME components (line 330-343), _build_table_payload builds the payload, then _small_result_to_markdown(payload) (line 1200-1223) returns non-None (a text line/bullet list) only when len(rows)==1, payload['truncated']==0, and 1<=len(columns)<=_SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS (4, per _SMALL_RESULT_MAX_COLUMNS usage), in which case a 'result_text' candidate replaces the table candidate (line 333-337); otherwise the normal table candidate is appended. _small_result_to_markdown (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1200-1223) explicitly returns None when payload.get('truncated', 0) != 0 (line 1213), regardless of row/column count. In components_to_blocks (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py), candidates are appended in strict stream order inside the single component-walking loop: TEXT components at line 327-329, DATAFRAME components at line 330-343 (a one-row/narrow result appends {'type':'result_text',...} in place of the table dict at line 335, at the exact position a table candidate would have occupied), and CHART at line 356-359. The second pass (lines 439-455) iterates `candidates` in the same order and, for each entry, appends exactly one block to `blocks` (text/result_text/chart), so the result_text block lands at the same index relative to text and chart blocks that a table block from the same DATAFRAME component would have occupied. Both the old table path and the new result_text path flow through the identical `blocks = _trim_blocks_to_budget(blocks)` call at line 478, which trims blocks by index/position (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:1070 area) without special-casing type, so the qualifying result_text block is subject to the same trimming-by-position as a table block would have been.

_compute_table_payload builds payload["columns"] = str_columns = [_coerce_cell(c) for c in columns] and payload["rows"] = coerced_rows = [[_coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) for c in columns] for row in rows] (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:907-920) — these coerced values are what the table block's cells hold. _small_result_to_markdown (lines 1200-1220) reads payload.get("columns") and payload.get("rows") directly (no re-coercion) and builds each line as f"**{_escape_small_result_text(col)}:** {_escape_small_result_text(val)}" for col, val in zip(columns, rows[0], strict=True) (line 1217-1219), i.e. it escapes the same already-_coerce_cell'd strings the table cell held, per the function's own docstring at line 1207 'Values are the payload's already-coerced cell strings.' This matches AC7 exactly.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:49 defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") which exactly matches the claimed character set (backslash, backtick, asterisk, underscore, brackets, angle brackets, tilde, pipe, ampersand). _escape_small_result_text (lines 1192-1197) first replaces \r and \n each with a single space (line 1194), then prepends a backslash to every character in that frozenset (line 1196). This function is applied to both column names and values when building the '**col:** value' lines (line 1218). Escaping '*', '[', ']' prevents markdown-it from interpreting '*x* [a](b)' as emphasis/link syntax, so it renders literally as claimed.

components_to_blocks (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:208-347) does a single forward pass over the component stream appending a {"type":"result_text",...} candidate for each qualifying DATAFRAME independently in stream order (line 330-335). In the emission loop (lines 444-455), every result_text candidate is unconditionally appended as its own {"type":"text",...} block (lines 450-453) with no merging/dedup/combination logic across candidates of that type. Thus two qualifying one-row results in one turn each produce their own separate text block at their own stream position, with any intervening blocks (e.g. answer text) preserved between them. This is directly pinned by tests/unit/test_format.py:1607-1618 test_two_one_row_results_each_get_own_text_block, which builds a stream of [_one_row({'a':1}), make_answer_text('between'), _one_row({'b':2})] and asserts blocks == [{'type':'text','text':'**a:** 1'}, {'type':'text','text':'between'}, {'type':'text','text':'**b:** 2'}] -- exactly two independent text blocks at their own positions, no merging.

col: a<b&c|d

' - i.e. literal <, &, | characters in the rendered HTML, not parsed as markdown/HTML syntax, consistent with CommonMark's ASCII-punctuation backslash-escape rule.
